takeaway: ADH is made in the supraoptic nucleus and rises with low arterial pressure or raised osmolality, not with high pressure. So the high-pressure statement is the incorrect one.

answer.text: Antidiuretic hormone secretion is stimulated by an increased arterial pressure.

lines.text: Antidiuretic hormone, ADH, is produced in the supraoptic nucleus of the hypothalamus.

lines.text: Osmoreceptors detect a rise in osmolality and switch it on.
In the kidney, renin is released when afferent arteriole pressure or sodium falls.
Aldosterone then drives sodium reabsorption in the distal tubule.
ADH is also stimulated by a fall in circulating volume or arterial pressure.
So high arterial pressure does not stimulate ADH, and that statement is the incorrect one.
